data.name: Skim Milk Powder
data.narrative:
Skim milk powder (SMP) prices increased at both ends of the range this reporting period. Processor prices were up from both last month and year-ago levels, with a 45 percent improvement year-over-year (YoY). Futures trading volumes increased 91 percent last week compared to the week prior. SMP futures weakened for October through January contracts, with the largest decline at 1.4 percent for December. Conversely, February and March futures contracts saw modest gains, increasing by as much as 0.4 percent for March. A major New Zealand dairy cooperative reported that the forecast total offer volume for SMP over the next 12 months remains unchanged. 

SMP prices at Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 414 increased across all offered contract periods, ranging from up 3.1 percent to up just over 5 percent. No product was offered for March or April. December and January accounted for 80 percent of total sales. Total volume sold was lower than Event 413 and year-earlier levels. Southeast Asia/Oceania was the top buyer, purchasing 49 percent of the total volume, which was up from 47 percent from the previous event and from 24 percent a year ago. North Asia followed with 39 percent. The SMP price reached its highest level in four years and was up 55 percent from year-ago levels.

data.name: Whole Milk Powder
data.narrative:
Whole milk powder (WMP) prices moved higher across the full price range, with the largest gain at the top this reporting period. Processor prices increased from last month, but are 3 percent lower compared to year-ago levels. Futures trading volumes increased 64 percent last week compared to the week prior. WMP futures were higher for all contract periods, with December gaining the most, up 3.7 percent. A major New Zealand dairy cooperative reported that the forecast total offer volume for WMP over the next 12 months remains unchanged. 

WMP prices at Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 414 increased across all contract periods offered, with each contract up just over 4 percent. No product was offered for March or April. December and January accounted for 78 percent of total sales. Sales volumes were higher than both Event 413 and year-earlier levels. North Asia was the top buyer, purchasing 54 percent of the volume, up from 45 percent at the previous auction but down from 58 percent a year ago. The Middle East bought 26 percent of the volume, followed by Southeast Asia/Oceania.

data.name: Cheddar Cheese
data.narrative:
Cheddar cheese prices weakened considerably at the bottom end of the range while strengthening noticeably at the top during this reporting period. Processor prices were higher than the previous month but remain 17 percent below year earlier levels. A major New Zealand dairy cooperative reports that the forecast total offer volume for cheddar over the next 12 months remains unchanged. 

At Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 414, cheddar prices were lower for all contract periods offered except November. The March contract, down nearly 12 percent, had the largest loss. No cheddar was offered for the April contract at this event. Total volume sold was similar to Event 413 and a year-ago levels. December and January accounted for 65 percent of all cheddar sales. Africa led purchasing, followed by the Middle East and Southeast Asia/Oceania. Strong global demand for whey protein products has driven higher cheese production, contributing to growing cheddar supplies and weighing on prices. As inventories and export volumes increased, cheddar prices experienced sharp declines.

data.name: Butter
data.narrative: Butter prices decreased at the bottom of the range, while moving higher at the top this reporting period. Processor prices decreased compared to last month and remain down 31 percent year-over-year (YoY). Futures trading volumes were down 28 percent last week compared to the week prior. Last week's butter futures were steady for February; weaker for November, December, and March; and stronger for October and January. A major New Zealand dairy cooperative reports that its forecasted 12-month total butter offer volume increased by 3,800 metric tons (MT) to 50,535 MT to align more closely with its anticipated product portfolio.At Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 414, butter prices were mostly lower, with January losing the most ground, down 1.1 percent. No butter was offered for March or April. December and January accounted for 82 percent of total sales. Butter volume sold increased compared to Event 413 and year-ago levels. North Asia led purchasing with 76 percent, followed by Southeast Asia/Oceania, and the Middle East.
